{{Quote|They're all over me! Get them off my&mdash;|A [[Clone trooper pilot/Legends|clone trooper pilot]] during the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]], being chased by a droid tri-fighter|<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref>}}
The '''droid tri-fighter''', also known as the '''tri-droid fighter''' or simply '''tri-fighter''', was a deadly [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy]] [[Droid starfighter/Legends|droid starfighter]] designed as a fast, agile and powerful space-superiority [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]], built to excel in [[Starfighter combat/Legends|dogfighting]].<ref name="ROTS ICS">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref> It would be used in large numbers throughout the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="Clone Wars">''[[Star Wars: Clone Wars]]''</ref>

==Design==
[[File:Trifighter_trio.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A trio of [[Droid/Legends|droid]] tri-[[Starfighter/Legends|fighters]] over [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]]]
The [[Droid/Legends|droid]] tri-fighter was designed by the [[Colicoid Creation Nest/Legends|Colicoid Creation Nest]]&mdash;makers of the deadly [[Droideka/Legends|droideka]]&mdash;and manufactured by [[Colla Designs/Legends|Colla Designs]] and [[Phlac-Arphocc Automata Industries/Legends|Phlac-Arphocc Automata Industries]]. The droid's ridged, three-armed design was based on the skull features of a fearsome predator native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Colla IV/Legends|Colla IV]].<ref name="ROTS ICS" />

The bracing arms surrounded the fighter's droid pilot housed in a rotating, gyroscopic core.<ref name="ROTS ICS" /> The droid tri-fighter had three independent thrusters, providing it with great agility, and a powerful reactor and control/[[communications transceiver]] that gave the craft unusual range for a fighter drone.<ref name="ROTS ICS" />

It was armed with one heavy [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannon]] protruding from the central ball, and a light laser cannon for each of the three arms. They could fire independently or together and could slightly tilt on rails to improve its deadly aim. Two to six missiles of variable payloads were housed within each arm.<ref name="ROTS ICS" /> The nose-like cannon made the droid tri-fighter similar in appearance to the [[DSD1 dwarf spider droid/Legends|DSD1 dwarf spider droid]] also used by the Confederacy.

The droid tri-fighter was capable of deploying [[Pistoeka sabotage droid/Legends|buzz droids]] via [[Discord missile/Legends|discord missiles]] fixed to the underside, and quickly became rival to the [[Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter/Legends|ARC-170 starfighter]] and the [[Alpha-3 Nimbus-class V-wing starfighter/Legends|Alpha-3 ''Nimbus''-class V-wing starfighter]]. Although it could not outrun the [[Eta-2 Actis-class interceptor/Legends|Eta-2 ''Actis''-class interceptor]] favored by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], it was bulkier and more heavily armed, making it a challenge for even the best living starpilots to overcome.<ref name="ROTS ICS" />

==History==
The droid tri-fighter was introduced into the [[Confederate Navy/Legends|Confederate Navy]] relatively late in the conflict, and its usage would further deplete [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] coffers.<ref name="ROTS VD">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> One of its first recorded uses was on [[Praesitlyn/Legends|Praesitlyn]], where they [[Battle of Praesitlyn|fought]] against the [[V-19 Torrent starfighter/Legends|T-19 starfighters]] of the [[Praesitlyn Defense Force]].<ref name="JT">''[[Jedi Trial]]''</ref> Tri-fighters were also deployed at [[Sullust/Legends|Sullust]], [[Saleucami/Legends|Saleucami]], [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]] and [[Belderone/Legends|Belderone]]. It would prove troublesome for even [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] pilots, as evidenced when three tri-fighters came close to overcoming Jedi ace [[Saesee Tiin/Legends|Saesee Tiin]] before being taken out by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]].<ref name="Clone Wars" />

[[File:Tris.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Tri-fighters in space]]
Many tri-fighters fought during the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]], where they destroyed [[Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter/Legends|ARC-170]] squadrons.<ref name="ROTS" /> Swarms of them also fought in the battle within the city, harassing Jedi and clone pilots.<ref name="Clone Wars" /> Following the execution of the [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]] by [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Sidious's]] new [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], these units were de-activated. A few years after the Clone Wars, a [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosian]] engineer by the name of [[Gizor Dellso]] discovered an old droid factory on [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]], and he re-activated the droids and created his own personal navy. When the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]] discovered his plans, the sent the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] to stop his plans. Many tri-fighters fought with the 501st in space. Dellso was later killed and the factory was blown up. At least one derelict tri-fighter was located in an [[Imperial junkyard]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="Rebellion">''[[Star Wars: Rebellion: My Brother, My Enemy]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Tri-fighter_CW.jpg|thumb|right|200px|An animated version of the droid tri-fighter]]
The tri-fighter concept at one point included snap-on booster rockets that increased the ship's speed and range for a limited time. With the boosters, the tri-fighter were essentially fired from a capital ship like missiles. Once within closing distance of enemy starfighters, the tri-fighter would jettison its booster and continue with an accelerated attack. Given the visual chaos inherent in designing the opening space battle, George Lucas ultimately nixed the booster concept, as it contributed unnecessary clutter and confusion on the screen.<ref name="DB-droid tri-fighter">{{DB|starship|droidtrifighter|droid tri-fighter}}</ref> 

In the ''[[Star Wars: Clone Wars]]'' animated series, a sleeker, more numerous variant of droid tri-fighters appear, armed only with a central cannon. These fighters swarmed the skies of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] during the battle leading up to the [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|third film]]. It is unclear if this is a different variant of the droid tri-fighter or simply a design error in the cartoon, which has come into conflict with [[canon]] in some other areas. It may also simply be a stylistic interpretation of the movie design.

[[File:Tri-fighter.jpg|left|thumb|200px|CGI model of a droid tri-fighter for ''Revenge of the Sith'']]
In ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]'', the laser cannon is replaced with a [[Chaingun/Legends|chaingun]] and is depicted as requiring a pilot to operate. The latter is most likely for gameplay reasons.
